q: The Jarzynski equality ⟨e^{-W/kT}⟩ = e^{-ΔF/kT} implies the second law ⟨W⟩ ≥ ΔF because:
opts: By Jensen's inequality: ⟨e^{-W/kT}⟩ ≥ e^{-⟨W⟩/kT} (exponential is convex)
The work W equals the free energy change
exp: Jensen's inequality for the convex function e^{-·/kT}: ⟨e^{-W/kT}⟩ ≥ e^{-⟨W⟩/kT}. Combined with Jarzynski: e^{-ΔF/kT} ≥ e^{-⟨W⟩/kT}, so ⟨W⟩ ≥ ΔF. The second law emerges from the convexity of the exponential.
